okNUMA: 6 node(s) (6 with CPUs), SNC 3 per L3, 2 socket(s) — up deploys the NRI balloons policy; label pods k3d-gpu.io/cores=replica for a balloon inside one NUMA node, memory pinned to it, near the pod's devices
infoRDT allocation (rdt_a: cat_l3 cdp_l3 mba) — resctrl classes are available but left off: the balloons policy ships control.rdt.enable: false because enabling it rewrites the host's /sys/fs/resctrl. To opt in, mount resctrl on the host (mount -t resctrl resctrl /sys/fs/resctrl) and set control.rdt.enable: true in nri-balloons.yml; usePodQoSAsDefaultClass then gives BestEffort/Burstable/Guaranteed pods 33%/66%/100% of the L3
infonoisy-neighbour isolation: rdt-mba — CAT + MBA can cap a neighbour's cache share and DRAM bandwidth through the RDT opt-in above (resctrl mounted: no); the shipped classes set cache shares only, so add mbAllocation: {all: ["50%"]} to the BestEffort class for bandwidth; the classes run inside the NRI balloons policy, which up deploys on hybrid or multi-NUMA hosts only
infoper socket: socket 0: DSA 4, IAA 4, QAT 0; socket 1: DSA 4, IAA 4, QAT 0 (no ARK default on file for this CPU)

doctor --perf

2 info 2 note 1 warn exit 0

CPU frequency (driver none)

good: cores ramp to full turbo the moment a request arrives: EPP performance or balance_performance, turbo on, no frequency caps — token generation is a latency-bound loop and every ramp-up shows in time-to-first-token

sources: https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/pm/intel_pstate.html#energy-vs-performance-hints, https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/pm/cpufreq.html

levelfinding
infono cpufreq policy exposed (VM or cpufreq disabled) — nothing to tune here
from
/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/

Uncore frequency (intel_uncore_frequency)

good: max_freq_khz at initial_max_freq_khz and min_freq_khz at initial_min_freq_khz: the hardware (UFS, or ELC on TPMI parts) picks the uncore clock inside the full range. A floor pinned high for decode is under test (EXPERIMENTS.md H29, PENDING), so it is not suggested

sources: https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/pm/intel_uncore_frequency_scaling.html

levelfinding
warnuncore00: max_freq_khz 1800000 is below the hardware ceiling 2200000
from
/sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_uncore_frequency/uncore00/max_freq_khz
why
a lowered uncore ceiling caps ring/LLC (client) or mesh and memory-controller (Xeon) clock, and token generation reads every weight once per token through it
apply
echo 2200000 | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_uncore_frequency/uncore00/max_freq_khz
revert
echo 1800000 | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_uncore_frequency/uncore00/max_freq_khz

Isolation for sandboxed agents

good: /dev/kvm usable for microVM sandboxes, each GPU alone in its IOMMU group, split-lock detection on, CET known, GPU observation streams limited to CAP_PERFMON

sources: https://docs.kernel.org/driver-api/vfio.html (IOMMU groups), https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.html (split_lock_detect), https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/sysctl/kernel.html (split_lock_mitigate), kernel source drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_perf.c and drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_observation.c (paranoid sysctls), Intel SDM vol. 4 335592-093 (IA32_S_CET 6A2H, IA32_TME_ACTIVATE 982H)

levelfinding
info/dev/kvm present: microVM sandboxes (Kata, Firecracker) can run here
from
/dev/kvm, /sys/module/kvm_intel/parameters/*
notethe CPU reports tdx_host_platform but kvm_intel runs without TDX (tdx=N): no confidential microVM sandboxes
from
/proc/cpuinfo (tdx_host_platform), /sys/module/kvm_intel/parameters/tdx
why
kvm_intel creates TDX guests only when loaded with tdx=1; stop running VMs and microVM sandboxes first, since modprobe -r kvm_intel fails while one holds /dev/kvm
apply
sudo modprobe -r kvm_intel && sudo modprobe kvm_intel tdx=1
revert
sudo modprobe -r kvm_intel && sudo modprobe kvm_intel tdx=0
noteno IOMMU unit registered: no DMA isolation between devices, no GPU passthrough into a microVM
from
/sys/class/iommu/
why
VFIO hands a device to a VM only with its IOMMU group; without VT-d enabled there are no groups
apply
BIOS: enable VT-d, then add intel_iommu=on to the kernel command line and reboot
revert
remove intel_iommu=on from the kernel command line and reboot
